incident_spec.summary: Performance degradation observed when adding TOP 1 to a query involving joins and ORDER BY.
symptoms: Query plan changes from Hash Match to Nested Loops with Table Spool
incident_spec.mechanism: Row Goal optimization changes the query plan, leading to inefficient execution paths.

value.sql: SELECT TOP 1 dc.DOCUMENT_ID, dc.COPIES, dc.REQUESTOR, dc.D_ID, cj.FILE_NUMBER FROM DOCUMENT_QUEUE dc JOIN CORRESPONDENCE_JOURNAL cj ON dc.DOCUMENT_ID = cj.DOCUMENT_ID WHERE dc.QUEUE_DATE <= GETDATE() AND dc.PRINT_LOCATION = 2 ORDER BY cj.FILE_NUMBER

schema_sql: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS DOCUMENT_QUEUE (D_ID INT PRIMARY KEY, DOCUMENT_ID INT, COPIES INT, REQUESTOR VARCHAR(255), QUEUE_DATE DATETIME, PRINT_LOCATION INT)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS CORRESPONDENCE_JOURNAL (CORRESPONDENCE_ID INT PRIMARY KEY, DOCUMENT_ID INT, FILE_NUMBER INT)
generation_sql: INSERT INTO DOCUMENT_QUEUE (D_ID, DOCUMENT_ID, COPIES, REQUESTOR, QUEUE_DATE, PRINT_LOCATION) SELECT n, n, MOD(n, 10), CONCAT('Requestor_', n), DATEADD(DAY, -MOD(n, 30), GETDATE()), 2 FROM generated_numbers WHERE n <= {row_count}
INSERT INTO CORRESPONDENCE_JOURNAL (CORRESPONDENCE_ID, DOCUMENT_ID, FILE_NUMBER) SELECT n, MOD(n, 5000), n FROM generated_numbers WHERE n <= {row_count}
